title: 2009 AMC 12B Problem 4
statement: A rectangular yard contains two flower beds in the shape of congruent isosceles right triangles. The remainder of the yard has a trapezoidal shape, as shown. The parallel sides of the trapezoid have lengths \(15\) and \(25\) meters. What fraction of the yard is occupied by the flower beds?

solutions.text:
The parallel sides differ by \(25 - 15 = 10,\) so each triangle has legs \(\dfrac{10}{2} = 5\) and area \(\dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 5^2 = \dfrac{25}{2}.\) The two beds total \(25.\)

The rectangle measures \(25\) by \(5,\) so its area is \(125,\) and the fraction occupied is \(\dfrac{25}{125} = \dfrac{1}{5}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The two triangle legs equal half the difference of the parallel sides
Each isosceles right triangle has legs \(\dfrac{25 - 15}{2} = 5\)
